matcher.scan.250kb.10k.note: Slice 14: tokens looked up by key, so 10,000 words cost what 1,000 do. About 47 ms locally (the old single regex took about 7.5 s here, research 06 F24); the browser's word segmenter is about 44 ms of it.

matcher.scan.ja.100k-nodes.5k.note: Slice 14's Japanese case: 100,000 text nodes of about 20 characters, about 1.5 words to swap in each. About 1.1 s locally, of which the browser's word segmenter alone is about 0.85 s, which slice 14's 300 ms didn't allow for. Text with no first character of any form is never segmented, and slice 15's time slicing runs scans in 8 ms batches; a typical page of 1,000 to 5,000 text nodes is 10 to 55 ms.

wordcard.cardFor.x1000.note: 1,000 word cards; one card's model is a thousandth of this, well inside 19 §11's 4 ms per open (DOM included).

speak.pickVoice.x1000.note: 1,000 voice choices over every recorded voice list (60 voices).

dashboard.groupAndIndex.5k.note: Slice 21: grouping 5,000 records into rows and building the search index, once per load.

dashboard.search.keystroke.5k.note: 21 §4: under 16 ms per keystroke for 5,000 words.

dashboard.search.keystroke.20k.note: 21 §4: under 50 ms per keystroke for 20,000 words.

dashboard.scroll.20k.x100.note: 100 scroll steps of the virtualized list with 20,000 words in jsdom; a step is one frame's work, so 3 ms each is far from 21 §14's 50 ms long task.

dashboard.open.20k.note: 21 §14: interactive within 800 ms with 20,000 words (jsdom, from script start to the first rows; the server's answer is excluded).

local.projection.build.5k.note: Slice 11 §2: building the content scripts' word list for 5,000 words.

local.projection.write.5k.note: Slice 11 §2 and its acceptance: building and writing it (into the fake storage area, which copies values like Chrome's) for 5,000 words.

precedence.pick.100k.note: Slice 18: 100,000 picks with no memo hits (100 pages of 1,000 distinct concepts, a 20,000-word vocabulary), each with cleanup, the concept, the language and the word. About 290 to 310 ms locally on a quiet machine (up to 460 under load), or about 3 µs a pick; the spec's 140 ms covered the language draw alone. A page makes one pick per distinct form, typically a few hundred: well under 1 ms.
